title: Custody Observability Matrix and Evidence Pipeline
content:
Overview:

This working doc defines a practical custody-observability matrix and a minimal evidence pipeline for KMS/HSM/BYOK operations that integrates with RBAC v2 and SIEM exports. Goal is to provide a concise, machine-validated audit schema and a set of lightweight automation hooks so ops and security can prove key lifecycle actions (create/rotate-disable/retire/escape) with cryptographically verifiable artifacts.

Scope and audience:
- Owners: security, infra-crypto, platform-engineering, and SRE on-call.
- Audience: SREs running key rotation, platform leads approving BYOK onboarding, security auditors, and SOC analysts consuming SIEM.
- Includes: RBAC v2 role mappings for key ops, audit event schema (JSONL), evidence artifact lifecycle (signing, archival, attestations), SIEM export and retention guidance, and emergency HSM failover play notes.

Design principles (short):
- Small canonical event model: every key-affecting operation emits exactly one canonical event per logical change.
- Evidence is append-only and content-addressed (sha256).
- Use least privilege via RBAC v2 for key operations, and require dual-actor confirmation for critical ops (retire/escape escrow).
- Automate cryptographic signing of evidence using an ops-signing key stored in an HSM-backed signing slot (not customer key).
- SIEM receives normalized one-line JSON per event for easy ingestion and query.

1) Custody-Observability Matrix (conceptual)
Roles (RBAC v2) -> Allowed key operations and evidence guardrails:
- key-admin: can create keys, configure rotation policies, and assign key tenants. Evidence: must produce create_event + initial_policy_snapshot signed.
- key-operator: can initiate scheduled rotation jobs, view key metadata, and run re-encrypt. Evidence: rotation_job_start + rotation_job_complete events.
- key-recovery: allowed to trigger emergency-unwrap with multi-approval; requires at least two active approvers from recovery-approvers group. Evidence: emergency_unwrap_request + approver_signatures (n) + emergency_unwrap_complete.
- auditor-readonly: read-only access to audit artifacts, cannot perform operations.
- infra-svc: service account used for automated rotation runner; limited by token scope to specific key IDs and rotation windows.

Mapping notes:
- RBAC v2 policies are expressed as verbs (kms:create, kms:rotate, kms:revoke, kms:escape) with resource selectors (tenant, environment, key_id prefix).
- Policy evaluation returns an allow/deny plus a required_evidence schema: e.g., require_dual_approval: true for kms:escape on production keys.

2) Canonical Audit Event Schema (JSONL line per event)
Field names (snake_case) and semantics (all fields required unless noted optional):
- event_id: string (uuid4)
- event_ts: string (RFC3339 UTC)
- actor_principal: string (subject from RBAC; e.g., user:ava.martinez or svc:rotation-runner)
- actor_claims: string (comma-separated list of roles/policies; optional but recommended)
- action: string (create|rotate|rotate_complete|disable|revoke|escape_request|escape_complete|policy_update|hsm_failover)
- resource_type: string (key|key_version|policy)
- key_id: string (redwood-kms://<tenant>/<key-name>)
- key_version: string (semver-ish or opaque id; optional for create)
- rotation_op: string (scheduled|manual|auto) (optional)
- hsm_slot: string (for HSM-backed operations, e.g., hsm-az1-slot3) (optional)
- evidence_blob_url: string (signed short-lived URL stored in SIEM entry)
- evidence_sha256: string (hex)
- audit_signer: string (signer key id that signed the event envelope)
- audit_signature: string (base64 of signature)
- prev_event_id: string (uuid4 of prior relevant event, optional but included for rotate_complete linking)
- human_reason: string (short free-text description; operator-supplied)
- additional_tags: string (csv; e.g., canary,customer-x) (optional)

Sample event (single-line, human-readable pipe format to avoid nested JSON in this draft):
event_id|event_ts|actor_principal|action|resource_type|key_id|key_version|rotation_op|hsm_slot|evidence_blob_url|evidence_sha256|audit_signer|audit_signature|human_reason|additional_tags
6f9b3c9a-9f4a-4a7b-b2c7-1f3a2b0b7e3d|2026-03-05T18:03:22Z|user:ravi.patel|rotate|key|redwood-kms://acme/payments/ps-key|v2|scheduled|hsm-nyc-02-slot7|https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-evidence/acme/payments/ps-key/rotation/2026-03-05.gz|b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184|ops-signer-v1|MEUCIQDx...base64...|monthly auto-rotate|pci,prod

3) Evidence artifact lifecycle
- Generation: For every event, the runtime collects a compact artifact: event_id, event_ts, action, actor_principal, target_digest, raw_log_snippet, config_snapshot. That artifact is serialized, gzip-compressed, content-addressed (sha256), and uploaded to the evidence S3 bucket under path /<tenant>/<key_name>/<op>/YYYY/MM/DD/<event_id>.gz.
- Signing: The upload triggers a lambda which pulls the object, computes sha256, signs the JSON envelope with an ops-signing key inside an HSM (or a KMS-protected signing key if HSM not available), then writes back a signed-envelope JSON containing: artifact_url, artifact_sha256, signer_id, signature, signer_chain. The signed envelope becomes the authoritative evidence blob.
- Indexing: The event written to the audit log (and SIEM) contains evidence_blob_url and evidence_sha256. SIEM ingestion pipelines must store both for integrity checks.
- Archival: Evidence objects move to cold storage after retention_threshold (default 2 years) while the SIEM retains metadata for the full retention period set by compliance.

4) SIEM export recommendations
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) compressed by day (gz). Each line is one canonical event.
- Fields to index: event_ts, action, key_id, actor_principal, audit_signer, evidence_sha256, hsm_slot, additional_tags.
- Enrichment: Add tenant alias resolution at ingestion time, and attach policy name from policy_id when available.
- Ingest targets: Splunk/Elastic/Datadog. Use the same field names in all sinks to simplify queries across tools.
- Integrity validation: SIEM scripts should periodically (weekly) pull a random sample of evidence_blob_url, verify sha256 and signature using the ops-signing public key (rotatable) and flag mismatches.

5) RBAC v2 enforcement patterns and token flows
- Tokens carry minimal scopes and a role set. The policy evaluator returns required_evidence constraints which the client must satisfy (e.g., require_approval_count: 2). The client-side rotation agent gathers approvals and emits pre-approval records that are then included in the canonical event.
- For BYOK onboarding: policy evaluator must ensure owner tenant mapping, escrow rules (whether Redwood stores a backup), and required legal-approval metadata. BYOK onboarding emits an onboarding_artifact that contains the customer_manifest (signed by both customer and Redwood operator).

6) Key rotation and emergency escape procedures (operator cheat-sheet)
- Scheduled rotation (day job): rotation-runner (svc account) claims rotation window, emits rotation_job_start, forks per-key rotation tasks, on success emits rotation_complete linking prev_event_id. Evidence: rotation report (counts, bytes rewrapped), compressed log, and per-version fingerprint list.
- Manual rotation: require user token with key-operator + reason. Evidence must include human_reason and ticket id (e.g., JIRA-1429).
- Emergency escape/unwrap: must be initiated via an interface requiring 2 approvers. Sequence: escape_request -> approver_signatures (attached to request) -> dry-run audit (simulated unwrap logged) -> escape_complete. All artifacts signed and stored.
- HSM failover: if HSM health probes fail for > 2 mins, runtime emits hsm_failover event and automatically switches to queued fallback (soft HSM - encrypted keys in KMS with restricted window). For any failover, the evidence pipeline must create a failover_report and trigger SOC notification.

7) Forensics and audit queries (how SOC will use artifacts)
- Query examples:
  - List all rotations in last 90 days for tenant X: index by key_id + action=rotate.
  - Find all emergency escapes: action=escape_complete and additional_tags contains prod.
  - Validate integrity for a production key: fetch evidence_blob_url from latest events and verify sha256 + signature.

8) Automation runbook snippets (operator-level)
- Quick integrity check (one-liner): fetch evidence blob, gunzip, compute sha256 and compare to evidence_sha256, then verify signature with ops signer public key.
- Recompute key material lineage: use prev_event_id chain to reconstruct version ancestry; flag any missing links for investigation.

9) Outstanding questions / open items (working list)
- Do we require signatures from both the HSM signer and a secondary cloud-KMS signer for high-sensitivity keys? (security: prefers dual-signature but ops cost).
- Retention policy granularity for BYOK (customer requirements may demand longer than platform-wide default). Suggest per-tenant override in policy.
- SIEM cost: tradeoff between full artifact content push vs pointer-only events. Recommend pointer-only with random sampling + spot checks.
- Integrations: need a deterministic mapping between RBAC v2 role IDs and SIEM actor_principal strings. Action item: eng-platform to add stable claim mapping endpoint.

10) Related artifacts and next steps
- Draft a small RFC with the proposed event schema and sample SIEM queries - link to ENG-4521.
- Prototype the evidence-signing lambda and test signature rotation scenarios (PR#1892).
- Run a chaos test: simulate HSM takeover and ensure failover emits hsm_failover + evidence artifacts and that SIEM alert fires.

Appendix A: Minimal signing envelope (human-readable, flattened):
- event_id: <uuid>
- artifact_url: <s3 url>
- artifact_sha256: <hex>
- signer_id: ops-signer-v1
- signature: <base64>
- signed_at: 2026-03-05T18:04:00Z
- signer_chain: HSM-v2 -> root-cert-2025

Appendix B: Onboarding checklist highlights (BYOK)
- Confirm tenant legal approval and export constraints.
- Verify customer-provided key material format and wrap mechanism.
- Decide escrow policy (none | encrypted-escrow | full-escrow).
- Capture customer manifest: tenant_id, owner_email, allowed_regions, retention_override, legal_ticket.
- Create onboarding artifact and sign by both parties.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact and developer-friendly. I want feedback on required event fields (should we include ip_address? process_id?) and whether dual-signature should be mandatory for production PCI keys.
- Ping: Ravi Patel for rotation flow validation, Maya Chen for HSM signer design, Diego Alvarez for SIEM ingest schema compatibility.

-- end of doc --
